title: The Ass in the Lion's Skin
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: An Ass found a Lion's Skin, and dressed himself up in it. Then he went about frightening every one he met, for they all took him to be a lion, men and beasts alike, and took to their heels when they saw him coming.

Elated by the success of his trick, he loudly brayed in triumph. The Fox heard him, and recognised him at once for the Ass he was, and said to him, "Oho, my friend, it's you, is it? I, too, should have been afraid if I hadn't heard your voice."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Ass find at the start?
options: A hunter's cloak
A pile of animal bones
A Lion's Skin
A discarded shield

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Ass do with the Lion's Skin?
options: He dresses himself up in it
He hides it away for later
He gives it to another animal
He tears it apart out of curiosity

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how do the men and beasts react to the disguised Ass?
options: They approach him to get a closer look
They laugh at his obvious disguise
They ask him where he found the skin
They take to their heels when they see him coming

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Ass do once he sees his trick succeeding?
options: He chases after the fleeing animals
He loudly brays in triumph
He removes the disguise to celebrate
He searches for a bigger disguise

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who recognizes the Ass despite his disguise?
options: A passing lion
The Ass's own owner
The Fox
A frightened villager

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox say would have frightened him too?
options: Everything, if he hadn't heard the Ass's voice
The sight of the Lion's Skin alone
The size of the Ass's shadow
The other animals' reaction to the Ass

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what ultimately gives away the Ass's true identity?
options: His unusually small size compared to a real lion
His slow way of walking
His inability to stand still while wearing the skin
His bray, a sound the Lion's Skin could not disguise

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Ass's triumphant bray undo his own success?
options: It attracts more animals to come and see him
His excitement leads him to reveal the very trait his disguise could not hide
It scares away the Fox before he can be recognized
It causes the lion skin to fall off completely

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "elated" mean in "Elated by the success of his trick"?
options: Filled with sudden fear
Filled with deep confusion
Filled with great joy or pride
Filled with quiet regret

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: A disguise can only hide your true nature until you reveal yourself through your own behavior
Lions are easily fooled by any convincing disguise
Foxes are the only animals clever enough to see through tricks
It is impossible to frighten others without real strength

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who does everyone believe the disguised Ass to be?
options: A wolf
A bear
A wild bull
A lion

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Ass do as he goes about in his disguise?
options: He searches quietly for food
He goes about frightening every one he met
He looks for the Lion who owned the skin
He avoids being seen by anyone at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Fox address the Ass once he recognizes him?
options: "Stop right there, imposter!"
"You've fooled no one, fool!"
"Oho, my friend, it's you, is it?"
"Take off that skin at once!"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox remain calm rather than fleeing like the others?
options: He has enough knowledge to recognize the truth behind the disguise
He is too far away to be frightened by the sound
He has already seen the Ass without the skin earlier that day
He does not believe in lions at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Fox's remark suggest about how convincing the disguise truly was?
options: The disguise never worked on anyone, including the fleeing animals
The Fox saw through the disguise immediately without any doubt
The disguise only fooled animals, never any humans
The disguise was convincing enough that even the Fox would have been fooled without hearing the voice

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the animals "took to their heels"?
options: They stood their ground bravely
They ran away quickly
They fell down in fear
They called out for help

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: An Ass is caught wearing a lion's skin by a real lion
A Fox helps the Ass improve his disguise
An Ass successfully frightens others in a lion's disguise until his own bray gives him away to the Fox
An Ass frightens the Fox successfully and is never discovered
